subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly token volume & peak TPS
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored hosted pricing range and, if helpful, a Dedicated sizing recommendation.

Recap from our conversation:
- Use case: conversational assistant + personalized recommendations for enterprise customers.
- API usage: mix of short chat turns and longer model outputs for summaries.
- Key requirements: predictable latency for peak business hours, cost target for planning, and baseline SOC2 controls (we can provide evidence).

What I need from you to finalize a ballpark:
1) Estimated monthly token volume (input + output combined). If you only have request counts, an average tokens per request (input + output) is fine.
2) Expected peak TPS (tokens/sec) or peak requests/sec during business hours.
3) Target budget on a $/1M tokens basis (if you have an internal target or guardrail).

Quick note on economics so we have a shared frame: hosted API unit economics are typically expressed per 1M tokens. For a rough planning exercise we map your monthly volume x ( $/1M tokens ) to get a monthly hosted cost. If you're after strict predictability we can discuss Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) where committed spend lowers unit costs and gives throughput SLAs.

I've attached a one-page pricing worksheet and a draft mutual action plan to speed procurement and sizing conversations. Once I have the numbers above I'll send a 2–3 pricing scenarios (hosted vs. 6/12 mo reserved commit) and loop in Sean for procurement/legal steps.

Would you be able to reply with the token estimate + peak TPS today or tomorrow? If easier we can do a quick 20-minute follow-up.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the docs. Here are the numbers we have today (estimates, happy to refine):
- Expected monthly tokens (approx): 20,000,000 total (12M input, 8M output).
- Average tokens per request: ~200 tokens (input+output).
- Expected peak: ~30 requests/sec during peak windows — with an average of ~200 tokens/request that maps to ~6,000 tokens/sec peak (so ~6k TPS).
- Budget target: we're aiming for roughly $800 per 1M tokens as a target to make the economics work for our pricing model. Open to adjustments if you have recommendations.

A couple of asks from procurement (Priya is looped):
- Any guidance on committed vs hosted pricing — at what volumes does committed start to make sense?
- SLA and support tiers for Hosted API (we may need a 99.9% uptime commitment).

If useful I can share a sample traffic curve (weekday business hours spike); that will help with capacity sizing.

Best,
Sam
Head of Product | Ava Labs
sam.johnson@avalabs.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Sam —

Appreciate the detail — this is exactly what we need to produce a useful comparison. A few quick clarifications and next steps:

1) Interpretation of your numbers: 20M tokens/month at a target of $800 / 1M => rough hosted run-rate of $16k/month (20 * $0.8k). We'll refine once we pull in model mix (different model families have different unit costs).

2) Peak TPS: you called out ~6k tokens/sec (6k TPS). That is helpful. For Hosted API that level of burst is generally handled by our autoscaling layer, but there are tradeoffs: higher bursts increase short-term spend (autoscale) and can expose latency variability at very short notice.

3) Committed pricing: as a rule of thumb, committed (Dedicated/reserved) starts to make sense when you have predictable, sustained volume and need SLA-backed throughput. For your 20M monthly baseline, we can run scenarios: hosted (no commit) vs 6- or 12-month commit with stepped discounts. I'll prepare 3 scenarios and include an estimated breakeven point for a 12-month commit.

4) Procurement asks: Sean will own the SLA/contract side; Priya, we'll include standard 99.9% uptime language in the term sheet and note available support tiers.

Next steps:
- I'll send a short hosted vs committed pricing comparison (3 scenarios) by EOD Monday.
- Dylan — can you add a quick note on any latency/throughput recommendations (caching, batching, avg tokens/request assumptions) so we can size a Dedicated pool if Sam decides to go that route?
- Sam/Priya — if you can share a weekday traffic curve that would help for peak sizing.

Would love to schedule a 20-min follow-up next week to walk the scenarios. What days/times work?

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Hosted API pricing qualification — expected monthly token volume & peak TPS

Hi all —

Quick engineering read on the numbers Sam provided:

- Peak math: Sam's peak of ~30 req/sec with ~200 tokens/req implies ~6k tokens/sec (6k TPS). If your 95th percentile request length is closer to 400 tokens, peak TPS doubles. Please confirm the distribution.

- Hosted feasibility: We can absolutely support this on Hosted API. Our autoscaling will provision capacity for bursts; however, you'll see variable latency during rapid scale-ups. To mitigate: enable prefix caching for repeated prompts, and consider client-side batching where possible.

- Dedicated sizing (if desired): for a steady-state baseline of 20M tokens/month with 6k TPS peaks, we typically recommend a small Dedicated pool sized for your 95th percentile token/sec and autoscale/burst headroom for the top 10% spikes. I can provide a numeric server/GPU recommendation once I have average model sequence lengths and the model family (e.g., Llama-2-13B vs. an LLM-70B family have very different kernels).

- Next ops steps:
  1) Share a traffic curve (Sam/Priya).
  2) We'll run a short baseline perf test on Hosted (simulate your peak for 30 minutes). We can provide test credits and a perf write-up.
  3) If you want a committed quote, we'll model a 6- and 12-month commit and show breakeven vs hosted.

Happy to jump on a 20-min session and run through sizing.

- Dylan
